question: Cholesterol from the liver is transpoed to the peripheral tissue mainly by:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cholesterol synthesis in liver" -> "Cholesterol packaged into VLDL" -> "VLDL converted to LDL in bloodstream" -> "LDL transports cholesterol to peripheral tissues" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Cholesterol synthesis in liver" -> "Cholesterol packaged into VLDL" -> "VLDL delivers triglycerides to tissues" -> "VLDL remnants converted to LDL" -> "LDL delivers cholesterol to peripheral tissues" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Cholesterol synthesis in liver" -> "Cholesterol packaged into HDL" -> "HDL primarily involved in reverse cholesterol transport" -> "HDL not main transporter to peripheral tissues" -> 30%

CHAIN: "Cholesterol synthesis in liver" -> "Cholesterol packaged into chylomicrons" -> "Chylomicrons primarily transport dietary lipids" -> "Chylomicrons not main transporter to peripheral tissues" -> 20%
analysis: The transport of cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues is primarily carried out by Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL). Cholesterol is synthesized in the liver and initially packaged into Very Low-Density Lipoproteins (VLDL). VLDL delivers triglycerides to tissues and is subsequently converted into LDL in the bloodstream. LDL is then responsible for transporting cholesterol to peripheral tissues. High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL) is involved in reverse cholesterol transport, moving cholesterol from peripheral tissues back to the liver. Chylomicrons are involved in transporting dietary lipids from the intestines, not cholesterol from the liver. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and the enhanced information provided, LDL is the main transporter of cholesterol to peripheral tissues.
